subject: General Test (Code: 501)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/General Test - 501.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)

The last 5 questions are a data-interpretation set based on one table; the set stays together.

questions.sub_topic: Body that publishes the Red List
questions.question: Which organisation publishes the Red List of Threatened Species?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) IUCN
Why: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), based in Gland, Switzerland, publishes the Red List, which grades species from "Least Concern" to "Extinct".
Why not the others: (A) is a conservation charity. (B) is the UN's environment agency. (C) is a treaty that controls trade in endangered species.
Key point: Red List categories include Vulnerable, Endangered and Critically Endangered.

questions.sub_topic: Leaders and their slogans
questions.question:
Match the slogans in List-I with the leaders associated with them in List-II:

List-I
(A) "Do or Die"
(B) "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"
(C) "Give me blood, and I will give you freedom"
(D) "Inquilab Zindabad"

List-II
(I) Hasrat Mohani
(II) Subhas Chandra Bose
(III) Bal Gangadhar Tilak
(IV) Mahatma Gandhi
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: "Do or Die" — Gandhiji, Quit India, 1942 (IV); "Swaraj is my birthright" — Tilak (III); "Give me blood…" — Bose, to the Indian National Army (II); "Inquilab Zindabad" — coined by the poet Hasrat Mohani in 1921 and made popular by Bhagat Singh (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Gandhiji and Tilak; (B) swaps Bose and Hasrat Mohani; (C) swaps Tilak and Bose.
Key point: "Jai Hind" was popularised by Subhas Chandra Bose too.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about Deepavali on the UNESCO list
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
A. Deepavali was added to UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in December 2025.
B. The decision was taken at a session held at the Red Fort, New Delhi.
C. It was the first time India hosted a session of UNESCO's Intergovernmental Committee for intangible heritage.
D. Deepavali was the first Indian element to be placed on the list.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A, B and C only
C) B, C and D only
D) A, B, C and D
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) A, B and C only
Why: A, B and C are correct: Deepavali was inscribed on 10 December 2025 at the 20th session of the Committee, held at the Red Fort from 8 to 13 December 2025 — the first such session hosted by India.
Why not the others: D is wrong: earlier Indian elements include Ramlila, Yoga, the Kumbh Mela and Durga Puja in Kolkata; Deepavali became India's 16th element. Options (C) and (D) include D; (B) leaves out the correct statement C.
Key point: Intangible heritage covers living traditions — festivals, music, crafts and knowledge.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about the Supreme Court of India
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court of India:
A. It was inaugurated on 28 January 1950.
B. It has original jurisdiction in disputes between the Union and one or more states.
C. Its judges retire at the age of 62.
D. It can issue writs to protect Fundamental Rights under Article 32.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B and D only
C) B, C and D only
D) A, B, C and D
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) A, B and D only
Why: A is correct: it was inaugurated two days after the Constitution came into force. B is correct (Article 131). D is correct: writs such as habeas corpus and mandamus.
Why not the others: C is wrong: Supreme Court judges retire at 65; 62 is the age for High Court judges. Options (C) and (D) include C; (A) leaves out the correct statement D.
Key point: Article 32 — Supreme Court writs; Article 226 — High Court writs.

questions.sub_topic: Body that adopted the WHO Pandemic Agreement
questions.question: The world's first Pandemic Agreement, meant to prepare countries better for future pandemics, was adopted on 20 May 2025 by:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) The World Health Assembly
Why: The 78th World Health Assembly, the decision-making body of the World Health Organization, adopted the agreement in Geneva. It will open for signature after an annex on sharing pathogens and their benefits is agreed.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are other international bodies; the agreement was made under Article 19 of the WHO Constitution.
Key point: The only earlier treaty made under Article 19 is the Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (2003).

questions.sub_topic: Time for B from work left after A
questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 20 days. A works on it for 5 days, and then B finishes the remaining work in 9 days. In how many days can B alone do the whole work?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 12 days
Given: A does 1/20 a day.
Step 1: In 5 days A does 5/20 = 1/4; remaining = 3/4.
Step 2: B does 3/4 in 9 days, so the whole work takes 9 ÷ 3/4 = 12 days.
Common mistake: taking 9 days as B's time for the whole work (option A), or dividing 9 by 1/4 (36 days, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Day of the week of 26 January 1950
questions.question: On which day of the week did 26 January 1950, the day the Constitution came into force, fall?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Thursday
Answer steps: count odd days up to 31 December 1949: 1600 years give 0; the next 300 years give 15, which leaves 1; the 49 years from 1901 to 1949 have 12 leap years and 37 ordinary years, giving 24 + 37 = 61, which leaves 5. Total so far = 0 + 1 + 5 = 6. Then 26 days of January 1950 leave 5. Total = 11, which leaves 4. With 0 = Sunday, 4 = Thursday.
Why not the others: (B) adds one odd day too many. (C) leaves out one. (D) misses the odd day from the 300 years and a slip in January.
Key point: Every 400 years have 0 odd days; each 100 years has 5.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about electricity at home
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about electricity:
A. Ohm's law states that V = IR, for a conductor at constant temperature.
B. Household alternating current in India is supplied at 110 V and 60 Hz.
C. In a series circuit, the same current flows through every resistor.
D. The earth wire protects users from electric shock if a metal appliance becomes live.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B and C only
C) A, C and D only
D) B, C and D only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) A, C and D only
Why: A is correct. C is correct: a series circuit has only one path. D is correct: the earth wire carries leakage current safely into the ground.
Why not the others: B is wrong: India's household supply is about 220–230 V at 50 Hz (110 V and 60 Hz are used in the USA). Options (B) and (D) include B; (A) leaves out the correct statement D.
Key point: Appliances in a house are connected in parallel, so each gets the full voltage.

questions.sub_topic: South Indian dynasties in order
questions.question:
Arrange the following dynasties in chronological order of their rise (earliest first):
A. Pallavas
B. Vijayanagara (Sangama) dynasty
C. Imperial Cholas
D. Satavahanas
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) D, A, C, B
Why: Satavahanas (from about the 1st century BCE in the Deccan), Pallavas of Kanchi (from about the 4th century CE), the imperial Cholas of Thanjavur (from about 850 CE, under Vijayalaya) and the Vijayanagara empire (founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka).
Why not the others: (A) puts the Cholas before the Pallavas. (C) puts the Pallavas before the Satavahanas. (D) puts Vijayanagara before the Cholas.
Key point: The Chola king Rajaraja I built the Brihadeshwara Temple at Thanjavur.

questions.sub_topic: State with the longest coastline
questions.question: Which state of India has the longest coastline?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Gujarat
Why: Gujarat has the longest coastline of any Indian state, with the Gulf of Kutch and the Gulf of Khambhat cutting deep into it.
Why not the others: (B) and (C) have long east-coast shorelines but shorter than Gujarat's. (D) has a shorter Konkan coast.
Key point: India's coastline touches nine states and four Union Territories.

questions.sub_topic: Records of the human body
questions.question:
Match the descriptions in List-I with the parts of the human body in List-II:

List-I
(A) Largest organ
(B) Largest gland
(C) Smallest bone
(D) Longest bone

List-II
(I) Femur
(II) Stapes
(III) Liver
(IV) Skin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Skin — the largest organ (IV); liver — the largest gland (III); stapes, in the middle ear — the smallest bone (II); femur, the thigh bone — the longest bone (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the skin and the liver; (B) swaps the stapes and the femur; (C) swaps the liver and the stapes.
Key point: An adult human skeleton has 206 bones.

questions.sub_topic: Collective noun analogy
questions.question: Bird : Flock :: Fish : ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) School
Answer steps: a group of birds is a flock; a group of fish is a school (or shoal).
Why not the others: (A) is used for cattle. (B) for wolves. (D) for bees and other insects.
Key point: The relation is member : group.

questions.sub_topic: Speed needed to save an hour
questions.question: A car covers a distance in 6 hours at 50 km/h. At what speed must it travel to cover the same distance in 5 hours?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 60 km/h
Given: distance = 50 × 6 = 300 km.
Step 1: Speed needed = 300 ÷ 5 = 60 km/h.
Common mistake: adding 5 km/h for each hour saved (55 km/h, option A); speed and time are inversely related.

questions.sub_topic: Largest of three consecutive even numbers
questions.question: The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 78. What is the largest of them?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 28
Given: numbers x, x + 2, x + 4.
Step 1: 3x + 6 = 78, so x = 24.
Step 2: The numbers are 24, 26 and 28; the largest is 28.
Common mistake: giving the middle number (78 ÷ 3 = 26, option A).

questions.sub_topic: Series with odd-number gaps
questions.question: Find the next number: 7, 12, 19, 28, 39, ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 52
Answer steps: the differences are 5, 7, 9, 11 — consecutive odd numbers — so the next difference is 13: 39 + 13 = 52.
Why not the others: (A) adds 11 again. (B) adds 12. (C) adds 15.
Key point: Rising differences of 2 often mean consecutive odd or even numbers.

questions.sub_topic: Developer of India's genome-edited rice varieties
questions.question: In May 2025, India released the world's first two genome-edited rice varieties, DRR Dhan 100 (Kamala) and Pusa DST Rice 1. Which body developed them?
options: A) The Indian Space Research Organisation
B) The Defence Research and Development Organisation
C) The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
D) The Indian Council of Agricultural Research
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) The Indian Council of Agricultural Research
Why: The varieties were developed by ICAR institutes (the Indian Institute of Rice Research, Hyderabad, and the Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi) using CRISPR-based editing with no foreign DNA added. Kamala matures earlier with higher yield; Pusa DST Rice 1 tolerates salinity and drought.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are research bodies that work in other fields.
Key point: Genome editing changes a plant's own genes; GM crops add genes from other organisms.

questions.sub_topic: Either-or conclusion in a syllogism
questions.question:
Statements:
Some cars are buses.
Some buses are trucks.
Conclusions:
I. Some cars are trucks.
II. No car is a truck.
Which of the conclusions follow?
options: C) Either I or II follows
D) Neither I nor II follows
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Either I or II follows
Answer steps: the statements do not show whether any car is a truck, so neither I nor II is certain alone. But I and II are about the same two groups and exactly one of them must be true: either some cars are trucks, or none is.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) treat one possibility as certain. (D) misses that the pair covers every case.
Key point: "Some A are B" and "No A is B" form a complementary pair.

questions.sub_topic: Total surface area of a solid hemisphere
questions.question: What is the total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7 cm? (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 462 cm²
Given: r = 7 cm.
Step 1: Total surface area = curved surface (2πr²) + flat circular face (πr²) = 3πr².
Step 2: = 3 × 22/7 × 49 = 462 cm².
Common mistake: giving only the curved surface (308 cm², option A), or the surface of a whole sphere (616 cm², option C).

questions.sub_topic: Economic indices and what they measure
questions.question:
Match the indices in List-I with what they measure in List-II:

List-I
(A) Consumer Price Index (CPI)
(B) Wholesale Price Index (WPI)
(C) Index of Industrial Production (IIP)
(D) Sensex

List-II
(I) Share prices of 30 companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange
(II) Output of mining, manufacturing and electricity
(III) Prices of goods traded in bulk
(IV) Retail prices paid by households
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: CPI — retail prices, used by the RBI for its inflation target (IV); WPI — prices at the wholesale level (III); IIP — industrial output (II); Sensex — 30 large companies on the BSE (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps CPI and WPI; (B) swaps IIP and the Sensex; (C) swaps WPI and IIP.
Key point: The Nifty 50 is the National Stock Exchange's index of 50 companies.

questions.sub_topic: Point dividing a segment in the ratio 1 : 2
questions.question: What are the coordinates of the point that divides the line segment joining (2, 3) and (8, 9) internally in the ratio 1 : 2?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (4, 5)
Given: (x₁, y₁) = (2, 3), (x₂, y₂) = (8, 9), m : n = 1 : 2.
Step 1: x = (m·x₂ + n·x₁) ÷ (m + n) = (8 + 4) ÷ 3 = 4.
Step 2: y = (9 + 6) ÷ 3 = 5. The point is (4, 5).
Common mistake: swapping the weights, which gives the point dividing in the ratio 2 : 1 ((6, 7), option A), or taking the midpoint ((5, 6), option B).

questions.sub_topic: State of the Bihu festival
questions.question: Bihu, celebrated three times a year with the harvest seasons, is the main festival of which state?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Assam
Why: Bihu is Assam's festival: Rongali (Bohag) Bihu in April marks the Assamese New Year, Kongali Bihu comes in October and Bhogali Bihu in January.
Why not the others: (A) celebrates Durga Puja and Poila Baisakh. (B) celebrates Raja and Nuakhai. (D) celebrates Yaoshang and Lai Haraoba.
Key point: The Bihu dance is performed to the drum (dhol) and the pepa (buffalo-horn pipe).

questions.sub_topic: Conclusions from late metro hours
questions.question:
Statement: "The city's metro will run till midnight during the cricket World Cup."
Conclusions:
I. Many people are expected to travel late at night during the World Cup.
II. The metro usually stops running before midnight.
Which of the conclusions follow?
options: C) Neither I nor II follows
D) Both I and II follow
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Both I and II follow
Answer steps: running trains late during the World Cup only makes sense if late-night travel is expected (I). "Will run till midnight during the World Cup" implies that this is not the normal timing (II).
Why not the others: (A) and (B) each leave out one conclusion that the statement implies. (C) rejects both.
Key point: A special arrangement implies both a special need and a different normal practice.

questions.sub_topic: Definite result from coded comparisons
questions.question: 'P @ Q' means 'P is greater than Q'; 'P # Q' means 'P is less than Q'; 'P $ Q' means 'P is equal to Q'. If A @ B, B $ C and C # D, which of the following is definitely true?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) A > C
Answer steps: decode: A > B, B = C, C < D. So A > B = C, giving A > C. D is greater than C, but D may be greater or smaller than A.
Why not the others: (A) is not certain, since D and A are not compared. (B) contradicts B = C < D. (D) contradicts A > C.
Key point: Decode the symbols first, then join the chain.

questions.sub_topic: Why aluminium resists corrosion
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Aluminium does not corrode easily, even though it is a fairly reactive metal.
Reason (R): A thin, tough layer of aluminium oxide forms on its surface and protects the metal underneath.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are true. Aluminium reacts with oxygen at once, but the oxide layer formed sticks to the surface and stops further attack. So (R) explains (A). Anodising thickens this layer on purpose.
Why not the others: (B) denies the link. (C) and (D) call a true statement false.
Key point: Iron rust, by contrast, is flaky and falls off, so iron keeps corroding.

questions.sub_topic: Weight of a body on the Moon
questions.question: The weight of a body on the Moon is about what fraction of its weight on the Earth?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) One-sixth
Why: The Moon's gravity is about 1/6 of the Earth's (about 1.62 m/s² against 9.8 m/s²), so a body weighs about one-sixth as much there. Its mass does not change.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) are wrong fractions. (D) confuses weight with mass, which stays the same.
Key point: Mass is constant; weight = mass × g changes with g.

questions.sub_topic: Assertion and reason on shadows
questions.question:
Assertion (A): An opaque object placed in the path of light casts a shadow.
Reason (R): Light travels in straight lines.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Answer steps: both are true. Because light travels in straight lines, it cannot bend round an opaque object, so the region behind the object receives no light — a shadow. So (R) explains (A).
Why not the others: (B) denies the link. (C) and (D) call a true statement false.
Key point: Rectilinear propagation of light also explains pinhole cameras and eclipses.

questions.sub_topic: Value of k for infinitely many solutions
questions.question: For what value of k do the equations 2x + 3y = 5 and 4x + ky = 10 have infinitely many solutions?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 6
Given: for infinitely many solutions, a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.
Step 1: 2/4 = 3/k = 5/10, so each ratio is 1/2.
Step 2: 3/k = 1/2 gives k = 6.
Common mistake: copying the coefficient 3 (option A), or doubling the constant term instead (10, option B); the second equation must be exactly twice the first, so k = 2 × 3.

questions.sub_topic: Ratio for mixing two kinds of rice
questions.question: In what ratio must rice costing ₹40 per kg be mixed with rice costing ₹55 per kg so that the mixture costs ₹45 per kg?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 2 : 1
Given: cheaper ₹40, dearer ₹55, mixture ₹45.
Step 1: By alligation: cheaper : dearer = (55 − 45) : (45 − 40) = 10 : 5.
Step 2: = 2 : 1. (Check: (2 × 40 + 1 × 55) ÷ 3 = 135 ÷ 3 = ₹45.)
Common mistake: writing the ratio the other way round (1 : 2, option B), which gives a mixture costing ₹50.

questions.sub_topic: Smallest country in the world
questions.question: Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Vatican City
Why: Vatican City, an enclave in Rome, covers only about 0.44 km². It is the seat of the Pope.
Why not the others: (A) is the second smallest. (B) is also small but larger than both. (D) is the smallest country in Asia.
Key point: Russia is the largest country by area.

questions.sub_topic: Direction of the hour hand on a turned clock
questions.question: A clock is hung so that at 12 noon its minute hand points north-east. In which direction will its hour hand point at 3:00 p.m.?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) South-east
Answer steps: at 12 noon both hands point to 12, which here is north-east. At 3:00 the hour hand points to 3, which is 90° clockwise from 12. Turning north-east by 90° clockwise gives south-east.
Why not the others: (A) turns anticlockwise. (B) turns 180°. (D) turns only 45°.
Key point: Fix where 12 points, then turn by 30° for each hour.

questions.sub_topic: Total votes from the winning margin
questions.question: In an election between two candidates, the winner got 58% of the valid votes and won by 1,440 votes. How many valid votes were cast?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 9,000
Given: winner 58%, loser 42% of the valid votes.
Step 1: Margin = 58% − 42% = 16% of the votes.
Step 2: 16% = 1,440, so the total = 1,440 ÷ 0.16 = 9,000.
Common mistake: treating the margin as 8% (58 − 50), giving 18,000 (option B), or as 58% of the votes (about 2,483, option C).

questions.sub_topic: Subject of the 2025 Nobel Prize in Economics
questions.question: The 2025 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, shared by Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt, was awarded for:
options: A) Experiments to fight global poverty
C) Studying why some nations are rich and others poor
D) Research on women in the labour market
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Explaining innovation-driven economic growth
Why: Mokyr received half for identifying, from economic history, the conditions for sustained growth through technology; Aghion and Howitt shared the other half for their theory of growth through "creative destruction". It was announced on 13 October 2025.
Why not the others: (A) won in 2019 (Banerjee, Duflo, Kremer). (C) won in 2024 (Acemoglu, Johnson, Robinson). (D) won in 2023 (Claudia Goldin).
Key point: "Creative destruction" — new products and firms replace old ones.

questions.sub_topic: Order of five stacked boxes
questions.question: Five boxes P, Q, R, S and T are stacked one above another. P is immediately below S. P is above Q. T is immediately below Q. R is neither at the top nor at the bottom. Which box is just above Q?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) R
Answer steps: number the places 1 (bottom) to 5 (top). S must be above P, which is above Q and T, and R is not at the top, so S is at 5 and P at 4. Q and T must be next to each other with T below: if R were at 2, Q and T could not be next to each other; if R were at 3, Q is at 2 and T at 1. So the order from the top is S, P, R, Q, T, and R is just above Q.
Why not the others: (A) P is two places above Q. (C) S is at the top. (D) T is just below Q.
Key point: Place the linked pairs first, then fit the rest.

questions.sub_topic: Source of the Directive Principles
questions.question: The idea of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution of India was borrowed from the Constitution of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Ireland
Why: The Directive Principles (Part IV, Articles 36–51) were modelled on the Irish Constitution of 1937.
Why not the others: (B) gave the idea of Fundamental Rights and judicial review. (C) gave parliamentary government and the rule of law. (D) gave a federation with a strong Centre.
Key point: Directive Principles are not enforceable by courts but are "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Article 37).

questions.sub_topic: Example of a non-renewable resource
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-renewable natural resource?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Coal
Why: Coal formed from plants buried millions of years ago; once used, it cannot be replaced on a human timescale.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) are renewed constantly by nature. (D) can be regrown, if forests are managed well.
Key point: Fossil fuels — coal, petroleum and natural gas — are non-renewable.

questions.sub_topic: Part of the eye that controls the light entering
questions.question: Which part of the human eye controls the size of the pupil and so the amount of light entering the eye?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Iris
Why: The iris, the coloured ring of muscle, widens the pupil in dim light and narrows it in bright light.
Why not the others: (A) is the light-sensitive screen at the back, where the image forms. (B) is the clear front window that does most of the bending of light. (D) focuses the light on the retina.
Key point: The colour of a person's eyes is the colour of the iris.

questions.sub_topic: Relation across four generations
questions.question: P is the brother of Q. R is Q's mother. S is R's father. T is S's mother. How is P related to T?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Great-grandson
Answer steps: P is a child of R (being Q's brother). R is S's daughter, and S is T's son. So T is P's great-grandmother (mother's father's mother), and P, a male, is T's great-grandson.
Why not the others: (A) skips a generation. (C) skips two. (D) gives the wrong gender for P.
Key point: Count the generations: T → S → R → P is three steps down.

questions.sub_topic: Sum when interest is a given amount less than it
questions.question: The simple interest on a sum of money for 5 years at 8% per annum is ₹1,200 less than the sum itself. What is the sum?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) ₹2,000
Given: SI = P × 8 × 5 ÷ 100 = 0.4P; and SI = P − 1200.
Step 1: 0.4P = P − 1200, so 0.6P = 1200.
Step 2: P = ₹2,000 (SI = ₹800, which is ₹1,200 less than ₹2,000).
Common mistake: setting 0.4P = 1200 (₹3,000, option A), which makes the interest equal to ₹1,200 instead of ₹1,200 less than the sum.

questions.sub_topic: Gas used to fill balloons safely
questions.question: Which gas is used to fill weather balloons and party balloons because it is light and does not catch fire?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Helium
Why: Helium is the second-lightest gas and is chemically inert, so it lifts balloons without the fire risk of hydrogen.
Why not the others: (A) is lighter but burns explosively in air. (B) is about as heavy as air. (C) is used in glowing advertising signs.
Key point: Helium is a noble gas, like neon and argon.

questions.sub_topic: Richest of five people
questions.question: Among P, Q, R, S and T, Q is richer than P, R is poorer than S, and T is richer than Q but poorer than R. Who is the richest?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) S
Answer steps: from the clues: S > R; R > T; T > Q; Q > P. So S > R > T > Q > P, and S is the richest.
Why not the others: (A) R is second. (B) T is third. (C) Q is fourth.
Key point: Join the clues into one chain.

questions.sub_topic: Host city of the 2030 Commonwealth Games
questions.question: Which Indian city was chosen in November 2025 to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games, the centenary edition of the Games?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Ahmedabad
Why: The Commonwealth Sport General Assembly in Glasgow confirmed Ahmedabad on 26 November 2025. The 2030 Games mark 100 years since the first Games at Hamilton, Canada, in 1930.
Why not the others: (B) hosted the 2010 Games. (A) and (D) were not chosen; Abuja (Nigeria) was the other bidder.
Key point: Glasgow hosts the 2026 Commonwealth Games.

questions.sub_topic: Players of both chess and carrom
questions.question: In a club of 50 members, 30 play chess, 25 play carrom and 10 play neither. How many play both games?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 15
Answer steps: members who play at least one game = 50 − 10 = 40. Both = 30 + 25 − 40 = 15.
Why not the others: (B) leaves out the 10 who play neither (30 + 25 − 50). (C) adds the 10 instead. (D) confuses "both" with "neither".
Key point: n(both) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A or B).

questions.sub_topic: Coding by reversing and shifting letters
questions.question: In a certain code, WATER is written as SFUBX (the word is written backwards and each letter is moved one place forward). How is RIVER written in that code?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) SFWJS
Answer steps: RIVER written backwards is REVIR. Moving each letter one place forward: R→S, E→F, V→W, I→J, R→S, giving SFWJS.
Why not the others: (B) shifts the letters without reversing the word. (C) moves each letter one place back. (D) forgets to shift the last letter.
Key point: Check the order of the operations (reverse first, then shift) on the example.

questions.sub_topic: Gases of dry air in order of amount
questions.question:
Arrange the following gases in order of their share in dry air, from the largest to the smallest:
A. Oxygen
B. Carbon dioxide
C. Nitrogen
D. Argon
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) C, A, D, B
Why: Nitrogen (about 78%), oxygen (about 21%), argon (about 0.93%) and carbon dioxide (about 0.04%).
Why not the others: (B) puts oxygen first. (C) puts argon above oxygen. (D) puts carbon dioxide above argon.
Key point: Carbon dioxide is a tiny share of the air but a powerful greenhouse gas.

questions.sub_topic: Discount percentage from marked and selling price
questions.question: An article marked at ₹1,200 is sold for ₹1,020. What is the rate of discount?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 15%
Given: marked price ₹1,200; selling price ₹1,020.
Step 1: Discount = 1200 − 1020 = ₹180.
Step 2: Rate = 180 ÷ 1200 × 100 = 15%.
Common mistake: dividing by the selling price (180 ÷ 1020 ≈ 17.6%, option A); discount is always on the marked price.

questions.sub_topic: Crop whose output fell from 2023 to 2024
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Production (in thousand tonnes) of four crops in a district, 2022 to 2025

| Crop | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wheat | 120 | 135 | 150 | 165 |
| Rice | 80 | 100 | 90 | 110 |
| Maize | 40 | 45 | 50 | 65 |
| Pulses | 20 | 25 | 30 | 25 |

Question: Which crop's production fell from 2023 to 2024?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Rice
Given: 2023 → 2024 — wheat 135 → 150; rice 100 → 90; maize 45 → 50; pulses 25 → 30.
Step 1: Only rice went down (by 10 thousand tonnes).
Step 2: The answer is rice.
Common mistake: choosing pulses, whose production fell in a different year (2024 → 2025).

questions.sub_topic: Percentage rise in wheat from 2022 to 2025
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Production (in thousand tonnes) of four crops in a district, 2022 to 2025

| Crop | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wheat | 120 | 135 | 150 | 165 |
| Rice | 80 | 100 | 90 | 110 |
| Maize | 40 | 45 | 50 | 65 |
| Pulses | 20 | 25 | 30 | 25 |

Question: By what percentage did wheat production increase from 2022 to 2025?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 37.5%
Given: wheat — 120 in 2022, 165 in 2025.
Step 1: Increase = 165 − 120 = 45.
Step 2: Percentage increase = 45 ÷ 120 × 100 = 37.5%.
Common mistake: giving the increase in thousand tonnes as a percentage (45%, option A), dividing by the 2025 figure (27.3%, option B), or giving 2025 as a percentage of 2022 (137.5%, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Average yearly maize production
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Production (in thousand tonnes) of four crops in a district, 2022 to 2025

| Crop | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wheat | 120 | 135 | 150 | 165 |
| Rice | 80 | 100 | 90 | 110 |
| Maize | 40 | 45 | 50 | 65 |
| Pulses | 20 | 25 | 30 | 25 |

Question: What was the average yearly production of maize over the four years?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 50 thousand tonnes
Given: maize — 40, 45, 50, 65.
Step 1: Total = 40 + 45 + 50 + 65 = 200.
Step 2: Average = 200 ÷ 4 = 50 thousand tonnes.
Common mistake: averaging the first and last years only ((40 + 65) ÷ 2 = 52.5), or giving the 2023 figure.

questions.sub_topic: Ratio of total pulses to total maize
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Production (in thousand tonnes) of four crops in a district, 2022 to 2025

| Wheat | 120 | 135 | 150 | 165 |
| Rice | 80 | 100 | 90 | 110 |
| Maize | 40 | 45 | 50 | 65 |
| Pulses | 20 | 25 | 30 | 25 |

Question: Over the four years taken together, what is the ratio of the production of pulses to that of maize?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 1 : 2
Given: pulses = 20 + 25 + 30 + 25 = 100; maize = 200.
Step 1: 100 : 200.
Step 2: = 1 : 2.
Common mistake: writing the ratio the other way round (2 : 1, option A), or using the 2025 figures only (25 : 65 = 5 : 13, option C).

questions.sub_topic: Wheat output in 2026 at the same growth rate
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Production (in thousand tonnes) of four crops in a district, 2022 to 2025

| Crop | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wheat | 120 | 135 | 150 | 165 |
| Rice | 80 | 100 | 90 | 110 |
| Maize | 40 | 45 | 50 | 65 |
| Pulses | 20 | 25 | 30 | 25 |

Question: If wheat production rises from 2025 to 2026 by the same percentage as it rose from 2024 to 2025, what will it be in 2026?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 181.5 thousand tonnes
Given: wheat — 150 in 2024, 165 in 2025.
Step 1: Rise from 2024 to 2025 = 15 ÷ 150 × 100 = 10%.
Step 2: 2026 = 165 × 1.10 = 181.5 thousand tonnes.
Common mistake: adding the same amount again instead of the same percentage (165 + 15 = 180, option B).
